label: negative
description: Hard negatives for the Phase 3 classifier eval. Every entry looks like a lifespan-intervention study to a naive keyword classifier and is not one. The 10 records in data/gold/ are the positives; this file is the other half.

categories.name: aging-no-lifespan
categories.description: Aging-related, but no lifespan is measured - biomarkers, biological-age clocks, healthspan endpoints only.

categories.name: lifespan-no-intervention
categories.description: Lifespan or survival is measured, but nothing is administered - observational, GWAS/QTL, natural variation.

categories.name: lifespan-adjacent-outcome
categories.description: An intervention on something lifespan-shaped but not organismal lifespan - cellular senescence, replicative lifespan of cells, organoids.

categories.name: review-or-meta-analysis
categories.description: Reviews and meta-analyses of lifespan interventions: the right words in the right order, no experiment of their own.

categories.name: wrong-organism
categories.description: Heavy lifespan vocabulary in an organism the project does not cover, or where 'lifespan' denotes something else entirely.

entries.title: Epigenetic clock in the aorta and age-related endothelial dysfunction in mice.
entries.reason: Builds and validates a DNA-methylation age estimator for mouse aorta and blood and correlates it with endothelial dysfunction; no animal's lifespan is measured and nothing is administered.

entries.title: A hematology-based clock derived from the Study of Longitudinal Aging in Mice to estimate biological age.
entries.reason: Trains a hematology-based biological-age clock on 2,562 mice and relates the aging gap to mortality risk and frailty; predicts age, does not measure lifespan, and applies no intervention.

entries.title: Fasting-mimicking diet causes hepatic and blood markers changes indicating reduced biological age and disease risk.
entries.reason: A real dietary intervention (fasting-mimicking diet) in a human trial whose outcomes are biological-age and cardiometabolic markers, not survival; its first sentence cites lifespan extension in mice, which is the trap.

entries.title: Natural variation for lifespan and stress response in the nematode Caenorhabditis remanei.
entries.reason: Measures heritability of longevity and stress resistance across natural C. remanei isolates; lifespan is an outcome of standing genetic variation, and no treatment is applied to any group.

entries.title: Quantitative trait loci (QTL) analysis of longevity in C57BL/6J by DBA/2J (BXD) recombinant inbred mice.
entries.reason: Maps longevity QTLs across 23 BXD recombinant inbred mouse strains kept to natural death; lifespan is measured precisely and the independent variable is genotype, not an intervention.

entries.title: [Association of matrix metalloproteinase 12 with all-cause mortality in Hainan centenarians].
entries.reason: Observational centenarian cohort associating MMP-12 level with all-cause mortality; a survival analysis with hazard ratios and no assigned treatment.

entries.title: hTERT Increases TRF2 to Induce Telomere Compaction and Extend Cell Replicative Lifespan.
entries.reason: hTERT variants extend the replicative lifespan of cultured human fibroblasts via telomere compaction; 'lifespan' here is population doublings of a cell line, not the life of an organism.

entries.title: Chronic DNA Replication Stress Reduces Replicative Lifespan of Cells by TRP53-Dependent, microRNA-Assisted MCM2-7 Downregulation.
entries.reason: Chronic replication stress shortens the replicative lifespan of mouse embryonic fibroblasts through MCM2-7 repression; the outcome is cellular senescence in culture despite the mouse material.

entries.title: Effect of Antioxidants on the Fibroblast Replicative Lifespan In Vitro.
entries.reason: Surveys whether antioxidants extend fibroblast replicative lifespan in vitro; both disqualifying at once - the outcome is a cell-culture endpoint and the paper is a review rather than an experiment.

entries.title: Sex differences in response to longevity interventions.
entries.reason: Discusses how males and females respond differently to interventions known to extend lifespan; the title is almost indistinguishable from a positive and the paper reports no experiment of its own.

entries.title: Rapamycin, Not Metformin, Mirrors Dietary Restriction-Driven Lifespan Extension in Vertebrates: A Meta-Analysis.
entries.reason: Meta-analysis pooling 911 effect sizes from 167 papers on rapamycin, metformin and dietary restriction; carries the gold set's exact vocabulary and every number in it is someone else's.

entries.title: Yeast Chronological Lifespan Model as a Tool for Screening Aging Interventions.
entries.reason: Review of the yeast chronological lifespan assay as a screening platform for anti-aging compounds; describes how lifespan experiments are run without running one.

entries.title: FAR-RED ELONGATED HYPOCOTYL3 increases leaf longevity by delaying senescence in arabidopsis.
entries.reason: A genetic intervention (FHY3) that extends 'longevity' in Arabidopsis - but the entity whose longevity is extended is a leaf, and the mechanism is delayed chlorophyll degradation.

entries.title: Changes in leaf lifespan, nitrogen resorption, and mean residence time of leaf nitrogen along a soil fertility gradient in an evergreen oak tree.
entries.reason: Measures leaf lifespan and nitrogen residence time along a soil fertility gradient in an evergreen oak; 'lifespan' is a leaf-level plant trait in an ecology study.

entries.title: Leaf Tissue-Specific Phosphorus Allocation Is Linked to Leaf Lifespan in Chickpea Accessions.
entries.reason: Links leaf tissue phosphorus allocation to leaf lifespan across chickpea accessions; heavy lifespan vocabulary attached to a crop-breeding phenotype.
